explanation: h(n) is the least L such that every interval (m, m+L) with m ≥ 1 contains distinct a_i divisible by the i-th prime for each i ≤ π(n) (HasPrimeMultiples, 0-indexed primes). Such an L exists, so sInf is the minimum; this matches erdosproblems.com/860. The page says Erdős–Selfridge proved h(n) > (3 − o(1))n. The docstring cites ErPo80 (19), which gives this as limsup h(n)/n ≥ 3, and the statement uses that infinitely-often form. It is a weaker but correctly documented rendering, and it is implied by Ruzsa's h(n)/n → ∞ in any case. Faithful.
